text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said it would be seeking a three-year wage freeze when it meets unions for negotiations due to start next Monday.
A spokesman for the German airline confirmed that Lufthansa chief Juergen Weber had called for such a freeze in an interview with the Stern magazine to be published this Thurday.

In an advance copy of the interview, Weber was quoted as saying that increasing competition in the airline sector and expectations of further cuts in airfares should in principle mean that wages would have to fall.
But Weber said that assuming the wage talks produced a workable agreement over three years he would be ready to offer employment guarantees and a plan for performance-related bonuses.
German cartel authorities earlier this week said they were investigating the prices Lufthansa was charging on its domestic routes.
